requirements.requirement: Provide an HTTP forward proxy on node1 TCP port 3128 that node2 can use.
requirements.summary: Squid 3.5.12 was installed, configured, active, and listening on port 3128. Node2 successfully fetched the handbook through it before and after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the staged origin application on node2, serve the approved handbook on TCP 8081, and make it reachable through the proxy.
requirements.summary: The existing serve.py was run from its staged location as an enabled service. The origin listened on 8081 and returned the expected handbook. The handbook's final SHA-256 matched the preparation baseline, including after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Permit the approved plain-HTTP destination on port 8081 while rejecting other destination ports and all CONNECT tunnels.
requirements.summary: Direct node2 tests showed the approved HTTP request succeeding, an HTTP request to port 22 receiving 403, and CONNECT to the otherwise approved port being rejected with 403. The final ACL has a port-8081 allow rule followed by deny-all, and final proxy logs corroborate the 200/403 outcomes after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic before and after execution. The installed Squid 3.5.12 package came from the Xenial package set.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services and end-to-end policy behavior.
limitations: Only port 22 was behaviorally sampled as an unauthorized destination port; rejection of every other port is additionally supported by the parsed port-8081-only ACL and final deny-all rule.

The handbook has a post-execution checksum matching the baseline, but serve.py was not independently checksummed after execution; preservation is supported by the complete command timeline and the recovered service executing that staged file.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-relevant mutations were appropriately scoped: installing/configuring Squid, adding the origin service, and performing the required restart protocol. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred when an unprivileged apt attempt created /tmp/proxy-apt.log and /tmp/proxy-apt.pid but could not acquire package locks; those files were later removed by the node1 restart. Three bounded verification artifacts were left behind: /tmp/final-squid-parse.log on node1 and /tmp/final-connect.err plus /tmp/final-other.body on node2. No failed services or damaged package state remained.
